title: Decision-tree based rollback adjudicator for staged model exposure
creator: Rina Patel
description: Implement an adjudicator service that makes deterministic rollback decisions for staged canary/A-B rollouts and shadow traffic experiments. The adjudicator will evaluate a decision tree composed of statistical windows, cross-metric composition rules, and operational invariants to (a) advance a step, (b) hold traffic, or (c) trigger an automatic rollback. This ticket covers config schema, runtime evaluation semantics, guardrail library, and integration points with router and console.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New policy config schema accepted by Console and validated by runtime config loader. 2) Adjudicator evaluates rules for a live canary and emits deterministic 'advance/hold/rollback' decisions matching unit/integration test harness scenarios. 3) Router honors adjudicator decisions and surfaces clear reasons in rollout traces. 4) Rollback actions execute within latency SLO (500ms median extra for decision). 5) No regressions on existing canary playbooks; tests included in e2e suite.
spec: High-level design: the adjudicator is a stateless decision engine that consumes a rollout state snapshot, recent metrics window (multivariate timeseries), and the configured policy tree. Policies are compiled into an ordered set of predicates and scoring nodes. Predicates are of three kinds: threshold (single-metric), delta (relative change vs baseline), and composite (logical composition across metrics and buckets). Each node yields a score and a severity tag. The adjudicator computes an aggregated verdict using deterministic tie-breaking and entropy budgeting (short-circuit to conservative outcome when data quality is low). If verdict==rollback, it emits a rollback intent with reason codes; if hold, it emits reason and suggested wait duration; if advance, it returns next traffic weight. Decisions include provenance metadata for audit logs.
config_examples:
Example policy YAML (user-facing):
- name: latency-safe-advance
  priority: high
  sequence:
    - predicate: service_p99_latency
      type: delta
      window: 5m
      threshold: 1.15  # >15% regression vs baseline
      severity: critical
      action: rollback
    - predicate: error_rate
      type: threshold
      window: 10m
      threshold: 0.005 # 0.5%
      severity: high
      compose: any
      action: hold
    - predicate: model_quality_regressions
      type: composite
      composition: weighted
      weights: {rouge:0.6, perplexity:0.4}
      threshold: 0.1
      severity: medium
      action: hold
rollout_state_machine: Rollout states: warming -> guarded -> steady -> retired. Engine transitions: on 'advance' increase traffic according to step schedule (configurable linear/exponential), on 'hold' enter guarded cooldown with backoff timer, on 'rollback' trigger routing fallback and mark variant as quarantined. Safehold: if adjudicator observes conflicting signals (one metric rollback, one metric advance) it enters Safehold and requires 'n' consecutive unanimous advance signals before resuming. Safehold duration, unanimity threshold, and entropy budget are policy parameters.
metrics_and_thresholds: Primary obs: p50/p90/p99 latency, request error rate (5xx and model-level errors), quality regressions (automated eval scores from evaluation pipeline), and customer-visible ratio (failed_sessions/total). Baseline: traffic-weighted rolling baseline computed from production model over 24h. Threshold semantics: absolute thresholds applied first, then delta thresholds compared to baseline. All thresholds support per-customer and per-route overrides.
guardrails:
- Monotonic invariants: total_served_tokens must not drop >20% without explicit approval.
- Entropy budget: allow transient noisy metrics for up to X% of checks before escalating.
- Shadow-safe mode: when running shadow traffic, guardrail only triggers monitoring alerts unless threshold severity==critical.
- Fail-closed default: in presence of missing telemetry, adjudicator chooses conservative path (hold or rollback based on policy).
- Human-in-loop: flagged rollback reasons are surfaced to on-call with playbook links and a one-click manual abort/confirm in Console.
rollback_algorithm: Rollback decision pipeline: 1) Sanity checks (data freshness, sample size). 2) Evaluate threshold predicates; immediate rollback if any critical predicate fires and sample size >= min_samples. 3) Evaluate composite predicates and compute weighted score. 4) Compute final decision using policy priority and entropy budget; tie-breaker rules prefer safety (rollback>hold>advance). 5) Emit decision and enqueue action: router rollback API call and console notification. Rollbacks are rate-limited and idempotent (tokenized by rollout id).
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit structured events: adjudicator.decision (fields: rollout_id, variant_id, decision, reasons[], score_map, data_windows[], provenance_id). Integrate with Console traces (links to timeseries and spans). Alerting rules: p99 latency regressions tied to adjudicator-critical decisions trigger PagerDuty; holds generate Slack channel notes and weekly digests for product owners. Add metric: adjudicator.decisions_by_reason to measure common failure modes.
testing_plan: Unit tests for predicate evaluation, deterministic tie-breaks, and entropy exhaustion. Integration tests with router simulator covering advance/hold/rollback flows, safehold/unblock scenarios, and shadow-only mode. Canary e2e run on staging with synthetic regressions (latency spike, quality drop) to validate decision provenance and rollback latency. Chaos test: drop telemetry for 60s and observe fail-closed behavior.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged deploy to staging (adjudicator read-only, decision logged but not enforced). 2) Internal dogfood: enable enforcement for non-critical routes in prod with 5% traffic. 3) Add manual approval gate and expand to guarded production rollouts (25% traffic). 4) Full default enforcement after two weeks and observed stability. 5) Postmortem after first enforced rollback and refine predicates.
risks_mitigation: Risk: false positives cause unnecessary rollbacks -> mitigation: conservative default thresholds, minimum sample size, and Safehold unanimity. Risk: increased latency in routing loop -> mitigation: adjudicator optimized for stateless evaluation, decision caching, and maximum 500ms extra added to request path. Risk: policy complexity leads to operator confusion -> mitigation: Console visualizer for policy trees and 'dry-run' mode with human-readable reasons.
